# Atlas {#sec-app-atlas}

```{r}
#| include: false
# knitr evaluates inline `r ...` only in a document that has at least one code
# chunk; the app links below are doc_atlas_url() calls (they follow this
# release's host and version), so without this they would print as literal text.
```

## Overview

The **Atlas** ([`r doc_atlas_url()`](`r doc_atlas_url()`)) is the MST's interactive application:
**one static web app**, built with Svelte and MapLibre, that runs entirely in the browser. Where the
[Scores](scores.qmd) and [Species](species.qmd) Shiny apps it replaced were server-rendered R
processes, the Atlas has **no application server of its own**: scores, flowers,
tables and reports are computed in your browser, by a DuckDB instance compiled to WebAssembly
(DuckDB-WASM) querying the release's published Parquet directly over HTTPS. It still depends on a
few other services for what a browser cannot compute itself — score and species map tiles come
from the project's **titiler**, zone outlines from **PMTiles** on S3, and the basemap from
**CARTO** — but there is no Atlas-specific backend.

On the public host the release is a query parameter (`?ver=v7`), resolved client-side against the
published `versions.json` and defaulting to the promoted release when absent. A `restricted`
pre-release is served only through the signed-in preview host, at
`https://preview.marinesensitivity.org/{ver}/atlas/` (the version as the URL **path**, since
Cloudflare Access scopes its reviewer policies by path, never by query).

This chapter describes the Atlas as of version 0.10.91. @fig-atlas-map shows the default Scores
view: the 0.05° cell grid colored by a composite sensitivity score across U.S. waters, dark theme
(the app's default). In the current build the four-tool rail is attached to the panel, which opens
docked on the left with Layers showing, the map's legend sits at the bottom right, and the
basemap's attribution is just under it.

## Quick start

**Desktop:**

1. Click a cell or a Program Area on the map. **Details** (the rail's second tool) shows its flower
   plot; **Add to report** keeps it as a place, and **Open table** lists its species.
2. Or open **Report**, and under **Add a place** choose a Program Area, pick one on the map, draw a
   **Rectangle** (click, move, click, then **Done**), pick from the gazetteer, type coordinates or
   upload a file.
3. Select a place in the list — Program Area or drawn — to see its results: a coverage note (or,
   for a Program Area, its published cell count, area and composite), a flower and component
   table, and (on request) its species table. Rename a drawn place inline if you like.
4. **Share** at the foot of the Report tool opens the place-link dialog — the fastest way to hand
   someone the same place.
5. **Open report** (the gold button at the foot of the Report tool) opens a printable, downloadable
   document (Print, HTML, ZIP or Word).

**Phone:** the tool rail is the bottom tab bar; use the Program Area picker or **Enter
coordinates** rather than drawing, and the file picker rather than dropping a file on the map
(that gesture needs a desktop pointer).

## Getting around

**The top bar**, left to right on desktop: the MST mark and title; a **release chip** that opens
the version picker; a **Scores | Species lens switch**; a **search field** (Program Areas and
coordinates in the Scores lens, @sec-atlas-scores; species in the Species lens); then, right-aligned
and icon-only (each shows a tooltip on hover or focus), **Share**, **Download** (a PNG or SVG of the
map view, a GeoTIFF of the current data layer, or a GeoJSON of the current places), a **(?) Help**
menu (Take a tour, keyboard shortcuts, a Docs link), **Feedback**, **About this release**, and a
sun/moon **theme toggle**. On a phone (below 900 px) the title collapses to the mark, and Share,
Download, Feedback, About, Take a tour, Docs and the theme toggle fold into one **More (⋯)** menu
beside a **search** button; below 381 px the mark hides too. The keyboard-shortcut list is
desktop-only. Report is not a top-bar control on either viewport: it is a rail tool.

**The tool rail** is four controls, always in the same order, in both lenses and on every viewport:
**Layers · Details · Table · Report**. **Layers** holds the map's layer stack and the lens's own data
controls. **Details** shows what was last clicked — the flower plot in the Scores lens, the species
information in the Species lens. **Table** is the species, zone and composition tables (the model
inputs, in the Species lens). **Report** is the Places flow and the report itself.

**The panel** that a rail tool opens is attached to the rail and docks on the left by default; one
header button moves both to the right, and the choice is remembered per browser. Resize it by
dragging its map-facing edge or with arrow keys, or collapse it to a small labelled pill; clicking
the active tool collapses the panel, and clicking any tool opens it. **Table** takes the whole stage
beside the rail (its "← Map" button returns). The panel's header says what is shown — the active
layer and unit, the clicked cell or species name, "3 places" — rather than the tool's name. The
panel arrangement is chrome, not part of the shared view: only the top bar's **Share** writes it
into a link (as a `ui=` token), the address bar does not carry it. On a phone the same panel is the
bottom **sheet**, with peek/half/full detents. On a desktop the map's **legend** floats at the
bottom right (mirroring to the bottom left when the panel is docked on the right), with a histogram
of the whole layer's values above its colour ramp and a marker for the clicked value; on a phone it
is a compact **Legend** chip above the sheet that opens the full legend, moving into the sheet's own
header at full height.

## Scores lens {#sec-atlas-scores}

The Scores lens shows the composite, extinction-risk-weighted score for every 0.05° cell (or,
aggregated, every Program Area) of U.S. waters. Opening **Layers** (@fig-atlas-layers) expands the
**Data** row into this lens's own controls — study area, spatial unit, the score layer, color
palette, a **Sphere** switch (globe vs. flat projection), and a **Cells outside Program Areas**
switch where the release publishes that overlay — above the rest of the **layer stack**, listed
top to bottom: **Selection** (pinned at the top), **Zone outlines**, **Data**, **Place labels**,
**Roads & buildings**, **Boundaries**, **Bathymetry** (present but disabled until a relief layer is
published) and **Land & water** at the bottom. Every row's visibility and opacity can be changed,
and most can be reordered — **Data** can never move above **Zone outlines**, so an opaque score
raster can never hide the boundaries it is measured against — and **Reset layers** restores the
default stack.

![The Layers panel, with Place labels moved above Data (one "move up" click) to show the reorder feature, and Data expanded to its study area, spatial units, layer and palette controls. Captured on an earlier build (0.10.44); the current panel's header shows what is on the map (for example "Score · Raster cells"), its header buttons move the panel to the other side and collapse it (there is no dock-bottom or maximize button), and the rail is attached to it.](/images/atlas/desktop-layers.png){#fig-atlas-layers fig-alt="A narrow dark panel titled Layers with four header buttons, listing Selection, Zone outlines and Place labels as toggle-and-opacity rows, then an expanded Data row with Study area (All US waters), Spatial units (Raster cells 0.05°), Layer (score) and Color palette (Spectral) selectors."}

Clicking a cell or a Program Area selects it: the URL gains a `sel=cell:<id>` or
`sel=zone:<unit>:<key>` token, which the **Details** (flower plot) and **Table** tools then
describe (@sec-atlas-flower-table). A click never switches tools: it updates Details in place and
adds a "Last clicked" row to the Report tool. A click on land or outside the scored area shows *"No scored cell
here"* with its coordinates and leaves the selection unchanged.

The top-bar **search field** also works here: it matches Program Areas (and any subregion/ecoregion
archive the release happens to publish) by key ("ALA") or by name ("Aleutian"), and coordinates
typed as "lon, lat" (e.g. "-140, 57" — "lat, lon" is read correctly too, either by an explicit
`lat`/`lon` label or because the default order would be out of range). Matching is entirely
offline, against only what the release itself already publishes — no Nominatim, no third-party
geocoder, no network call. Choosing a Program Area result selects it exactly as clicking it on the
map would, and flies the camera there; choosing a coordinate result flies to the point and selects
that cell. Results are a keyboard-navigable list (arrow keys, Enter to select, Esc to close), on
both the desktop top-bar field and the phone's search modal.

## Species lens

Switching to **Species** turns the top-bar search into a species picker (common or scientific
name, with an "Only species in US waters" checkbox). **Layers** then leads with a **Model input**
picker — the merged model as a filled pill marked **✓** with a gold edge, plus one pill per
contributing input dataset — a **Zoom to layer on change** checkbox (on by default; picking an input
refits the camera to that surface, and `zl=0` in the link turns it off), and, where the selected
input publishes both, a labelled **Show … as** switch ("Original" vs. "Interpolated," or "Delivered"
vs. "As ingested" for a dataset already on the scoring grid). Below it the **Data** row carries the
species title with its zoom actions. An input's raster is found the way the retired Species Shiny
app found it — through the release's **model-asset registry**, looked up by model key — and an input
whose registry row is missing renders as a **struck-through, non-interactive pill**, never simply
omitted. The species' own information — names, ESA listing, IUCN Red List category, WoRMS id, and the
tree of values (the merged model and its inputs, the layer on screen in bold) — is in **Details**.
Selecting a species flies the map to that model's extent; clicking it then returns that cell's
modelled value, or *"No scored cell here"* outside the model's range. The legend floats in a corner
of the map (a legend chip on a phone), titled with the species' common and scientific name, with a
subtitle naming the layer and its 1–100 range.

![The Species lens' Layers panel for the leatherback turtle (*Dermochelys coriacea*): the merged model with every one of its six inputs struck through. Captured on an earlier build (before 0.10.78), when v7's app bundle had not yet been republished and every input showed struck through; on the live Atlas all six inputs are available. The current Layers panel also leads with a "Model input" picker and a "Zoom to layer on change" checkbox, and the species information shown below the pills here is now in the Details tool.](/images/atlas/desktop-species.png){#fig-atlas-species fig-alt="A narrow dark panel titled Layers with the Selection, Zone outlines and an expanded Data row: the title Dermochelys coriacea and Leatherback Turtle, a gold-edged box with a checked Merged Model pill and six struck-through input pills (AquaMaps SDM, NMFS Critical Habitat, FWS Critical Habitat, FWS Range, IUCN Range, SWOT+DPS Turtle Range), then the species facts: ESA listing, IUCN Red List, WoRMS id."}

## Places {#sec-atlas-places}

**Places** — the first part of the **Report** tool, listed with its count ("Places 2 / 20") above
an **Add a place** section — is what the two retired Shiny apps did not have: any area you outline
gets the same scores and species results the built-in Program Areas get. The empty state reads
exactly: *"No places yet. Click the map, or add one below."* A click on the map shows up as a pink
**Last clicked** row with an **Add** button, which hides once that place is in the list; a click
never wipes places you have explicitly added.

- **Pick a Program Area.** The **Add a Program Area** chooser plus **Add this Program Area** needs no
  pointer and works on a phone. Or turn on **Pick mode** and click on the map — that only highlights
  it (Ctrl/Cmd-click, Shift-click or long-press to highlight several) — and **"Add to places (n)"**
  is the button that actually adds it; several picks become **one** place. Program Areas are shown as
  **"Full Name (KEY)"** — e.g. "St. George Basin (GEO)" — from an app-side name table generated off
  the canonical Program-Area geometry (no published release, v6 through v9, actually publishes a
  full name on its own Program Area rows; a release that does publish one is preferred when
  present), everywhere: Places, search, the map tooltip, the Details flower's title, the Table
  header, the Zones table and the report.
- **Pick from the gazetteer.** Turn on **Pick from gazetteer** to show the gazetteer's polygons on the
  map and click one to add it. The place is carried in the link by its gazetteer id, not its outline
  (@sec-atlas-place-links); other gazetteer collections appear in a **Gazetteer layer** selector once
  the gazetteer publishes its layer list, and the map's credit line names the gazetteer's data while
  its polygons or places are shown.
- **Draw** a Polygon, Rectangle or Circle: **click, move, click** for each vertex or corner (not a
  drag), then press **Done** — a polygon also closes when you click its first vertex again, or
  press Enter. A circle is stored as a 64-sided polygon. Dragging a finished shape's corner **edits
  that place in place** (same row, same name, re-analysed) rather than adding a new one.
- **Enter coordinates** — the keyboard/screen-reader alternative to drawing, in a modal dialog: a
  bounding box (`xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax`), a list of `lon, lat` vertices one per line, or pasted
  WKT/GeoJSON. A refusal is shown verbatim — what went wrong, why, and how to fix it.
- **Upload a file**, through the picker or by dropping it anywhere on the map: *"GeoJSON, zipped
  shapefile, KML, GPX, FlatGeobuf, WKT or GeoPackage, up to 10 MB."* **GeoPackage** is now read
  (polygons only, same as every other format), through the same resident DuckDB-WASM engine the
  scores boot, via its `spatial` extension — fetched live, with consent, from
  `extensions.duckdb.org` (the one deliberately non-mirrored third-party download, 22.4 MB); each
  `.gpkg` upload asks first, not just the first one in a session. A GeoPackage with no
  vector layer (raster tiles, or a plain attribute table) is refused when `ST_Read` fails to read
  it (see Known limitations), not by a dedicated check. Other rules that cause a refusal: polygons
  only (points and lines are refused, never buffered); a shapefile needs its `.prj` (projected
  coordinates are refused); at most 50,000 vertices; a zipped shapefile at most 50 MB uncompressed
  and 200 entries; and the shape must touch the U.S. study area. A feature's own name (KML's
  `<name>`, or a `name`/`title`/`label` property on GeoJSON/shapefile/etc., case-insensitive) —
  auto-detected from the file's **first** feature and applied to every feature — names each place;
  a file with no such property falls back to the file name, numbered. A file with several features
  becomes one place per feature (up to 20), each named this way, or one merged place, named after
  the file, your choice.

![The Places panel with two places, both analysed: a Program Area ("Aleutian Arc (ALA)," 875,225 km², 28.3 composite) and a selected, entered-coordinates place ("bounding box," 98,973 km², 100% coverage, 27.1 composite) whose coverage note reads "100.0% of this place is inside the US study area (3,600 of 3,600 cells)"; the drop zone above the list names the accepted formats, GeoPackage included. Captured on 0.10.62; since 0.10.83 this list sits at the top of the Report tool, above an "Add a place" section, not in a separate Places tab.](/images/atlas/desktop-places.png){#fig-atlas-places fig-alt="Desktop Places panel listing Aleutian Arc (ALA) at 28.3 composite and a typed bounding-box place at 27.1 composite with 100% coverage, the bounding box outlined in pink on the Gulf of Mexico map, and a file drop zone reading GeoJSON, zipped shapefile, KML, GPX, FlatGeobuf, WKT or GeoPackage, up to 10 MB."}

![The "Enter coordinates" dialog, showing a refusal for input that matches none of the three accepted shapes. Captured on an earlier build (0.10.44) and not recaptured since.](/images/atlas/desktop-coordinate-dialog.png){#fig-atlas-coords fig-alt="A dialog titled Enter coordinates with a text box holding a single longitude, latitude point, and a refusal message below it saying what shapes were expected instead."}

Each row shows its area and, as soon as it is analysed, its data coverage percentage and composite
score directly in the row — for a **drawn, typed or uploaded** place the same analysis runs for
every such place in the list, not only the one currently selected; a **Program Area** row shows
its own published composite the same way (e.g. "Aleutian Arc (ALA) … 28.3 composite"). Row actions:
an inline **rename** (≤ 60 characters, drawn/uploaded places only), **zoom to**, **duplicate**
(drawn/uploaded only), **delete**, and **Open in report**. Selecting **any** place — drawn, typed,
uploaded, or a **Program Area** — expands the same **results** panel below the list, though the
note at its top differs by kind: a drawn, typed or uploaded place shows a coverage note ("*N*% of
this place is inside the US study area (*a* of *b* cells)", or "This place is outside US waters
here: no scores can be computed"); a Program Area shows its own note instead ("*N* cells, *A* km²;
published composite *C*."). Both then show a flower plot and a component table, and a species
table on request — a drawn/typed/uploaded place behind a "Loading species needs *N* tiles, about
*X* MB. Continue?" prompt (species come from map tiles), a Program Area behind a plain **Load
species** button with no such prompt (its species table is a precomputed release table, not
tiles). A single selected Program Area reads all of this straight off the release (the same path
the Scores lens's **Table › Zones** tool uses, @sec-atlas-flower-table); a multi-Program-Area
selection (several picks added as one place) still sums area and means the composite for the list
row, but its flower/component/species panel asks you to select a single Program Area instead of
guessing which one's to draw. **Show analysis cells** paints the analysed 0.05° cells (up to 20,000
of them) for a drawn, typed or uploaded place; for a Program Area it reads plainly *"Show analysis
cells: not available for Program Areas yet"* — the app bundle the Atlas reads does not yet carry
per-zone cells, even though the release's own tables do (see Known limitations) — rather than
showing a disabled control with a misleading reason. The list caps at 20 places ("*n* / 20
places"); **Recent** (this browser only) offers to add a removed place back. The Report
tool's footer is pinned to the bottom of the pane: a sentence saying what the report is about
("Reporting on 2 places.", "Reporting on the last clicked place. Add it to keep it.", or "Add a
place to open a report."), the gold **Open report** button (disabled with nothing to report on),
then **Share** and **Download places** (GeoJSON, with each gazetteer place's id), the last two
disabled with zero places.

**Two different Share buttons.** The top-bar **Share** simply copies the current address to the
clipboard, plus a `ui=` token that records the panel arrangement — no dialog, no summary, no length
check. The **Share** at the foot of the Report tool opens the real dialog described next, and is the
one to use whenever places are involved.

## How places are stored in the link {#sec-atlas-place-links}

A place never lives on a server: it is encoded directly into the URL fragment (`#pl=`, never the
query string, so it is never sent to a server or a referrer), so opening a shared link reproduces
the sender's exact area. Every analysis runs on the **decoded** geometry, never the geometry as
drawn, so the numbers can never diverge between sender and recipient. Places are joined with `~`:

```
#pl=z.pa.GAA~g1.Gulf%20box.EAMBAQSf_grYrQPQDwAA0A_PDwA~p.NMS%3ACINMS.Channel%20Islands
```
(the decoded form; the address bar itself percent-encodes `~` and other reserved characters)

- **`z.<set>.<key>[,<key>...]`** — a reference to a *built-in* zone (`pa` Program Area, `pl`
  Planning Area, `er` ecoregion, `sr` subregion); its geometry comes from the release's own
  PMTiles.
- **`g1.<name>.<base64url bytes>`** — a drawn, typed or uploaded polygon, carried inline as a
  compact binary encoding (see "For developers" below).
- **`p.<place_id>.<name>`** — a gazetteer place, carried **by reference**: only the gazetteer's
  `place_id` and a display name travel, e.g. `p.NMS%3ACINMS.Channel%20Islands`. It is fetched when
  the link opens and analysed like a drawn place; if the gazetteer cannot be reached the place stays
  in the list (and the link) with a "couldn't load" note and a Retry. Links made before 0.10.88 open
  unchanged, but an older Atlas drops a `p.` place it cannot read.
- **`u.<name>.<8-hex-digit digest>`** — the fallback for a place too large to carry (see below):
  only a name and a digest travel.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## For developers: the `g1` byte layout

Each ring is quantized to a fixed precision (3 decimal digits, ~110 m — 4 digits when the place's
bounding box is under 0.5° in **both** directions), delta-encoded vertex-to-vertex as zigzag
varints running across rings and polygons, and base64url-encoded with no general-purpose
compression (delta varints are already dense). Longitudes are stored unwrapped, so a place crossing
the antimeridian round-trips without a special case. `msens::place_decode()` is the R decoder; the
shared test fixture (`tests/fixtures/place_codec.json`) matches it byte for byte.
:::

**The link's length is checked only when you open the Report tool's Share dialog.** Adding a place, or copying the
top-bar Share link, carries the unsimplified geometry (already quantized to 3–4 decimals) regardless
of length. In that dialog: up to **2,000 characters** silently; between 2,000 and 8,000 a note reads
"This link is over 2,000 characters — some chat apps and older browsers truncate very long links,"
with **Copy anyway**; only **above 8,000** does the Douglas-Peucker ladder run — 0.001° doubling to
0.016°, a rung accepted only while the area changes by no more than 1% and every ring stays simple —
**aiming to bring the link back under 2,000 characters**; it stops at the first rung that does, or,
if none does, uses the coarsest accepted rung provided that still fits under 8,000. This is never
silent: the dialog shows the before/after (vertices, area change, cells, @fig-atlas-share-ladder),
and you click **"Simplify and update the numbers"** to accept it — which is also what rewrites
`#pl=`, so the copied link and the displayed numbers can never disagree. If even the coarsest rung
is still too long, **Copy link anyway** copies **every** drawn, typed or uploaded place (zone places
are unaffected) as a `u.` token instead — your own address bar and session keep the real shapes; the
recipient of that copied link sees a named row with no results and a "not analysed yet" chip, never
a prompt. The dialog's own advice at that point is to **download the place as GeoJSON** and send
that alongside the link. A single small rectangle almost always fits in the silent budget; that is
not guaranteed for several places together, or a long base URL.

![The Share dialog: what the link carries and its exact length. Captured on an earlier build (0.10.44) and not recaptured since; the dialog is opened from the Share button at the foot of the Report tool.](/images/atlas/desktop-share-dialog.png){#fig-atlas-share fig-alt="A small dialog titled Share with a one-sentence summary of what the link carries, its length in characters, and a Copy link button."}

![The Share dialog's simplification ladder for an oversized place: before/after vertex count, area change and cell count, with a "Simplify and update the numbers" button. Captured on an earlier build (0.10.44) and not recaptured since.](/images/atlas/desktop-share-ladder.png){#fig-atlas-share-ladder fig-alt="The Share dialog reading link length 1,564 characters, with the text: Simplifying to 0.004 degrees would change this place from 3501 to 411 vertices (-0.03% area, 12059 to 12055 cells), and a Simplify and update the numbers button."}

The rest of the view travels the same URL-is-the-state way, in the query string: `ver`, `lens`,
`lyr`/`sp` (with `in`, `rep` and `us` for a species' input, representation and US-waters filter),
`unit`, `area`, `map` (camera), `pal`, `sel`, `layers` (the stack deltas from
@sec-atlas-scores), `zl` (zoom to layer), `theme` and `tour` — each written only when it differs
from its default. `?tool=report` (or `layers`, `details`, `table`) opens that rail tool and counts as a deep link, so the
first-visit welcome does not cover it; the top-bar Share adds a `ui=` token for the panel
arrangement. A link from the retired Shiny apps (`mdl_key`, `mdl_seq`) is rewritten to `sp` (and
`in` when it named an input) when the Atlas loads.

## Details and Table {#sec-atlas-flower-table}

**Details** (the rail's second tool) describes what was last clicked, and is the same tool in both
lenses. In the Scores lens it is the **Flower plot** for the clicked cell or Program Area, headed by
its subject ("Cell 3372565 · 28.275° N, 83.575° W" or the Program Area's full name), with **Add to
report** and **Open table** buttons; with nothing clicked it asks you to select a cell or an area. In
the Species lens it is the species' information (see the Species lens above). A drawn place's flower
and species table live in the Report tool's results panel instead (@sec-atlas-places).

The flower draws one equal-width annular petal per score component, scaled to its rescaled score;
the hub shows the **plain mean** of the components present (not a weighted mean). Since 0.10.41 the
values also list in a real table (swatch, component, score, and a Mean row) below the plot.

![The Flower plot for a clicked cell in the Gulf of America: one petal per score component, and the values table with a Mean row below it. Captured on an earlier build (0.10.44), when the flower had its own rail tool titled "Flower plot"; it now opens under Details, headed by the clicked cell's subject line.](/images/atlas/desktop-flower.png){#fig-atlas-flower fig-alt="A narrow dark panel titled Flower plot, headed by a cell id and coordinates, with a flower of eight colored petals of different lengths around a hub reading 51, and below it a table of Bird 81.4, Coral 34.0, Fish 51.4, Invertebrate 56.5, Mammal 12.0, Other 73.4, Turtle 93.6, Primary producer 9.4 and a Mean row of 51."}

**Table** takes the whole stage beside the rail, with a one-row header: a **← Map** button that collapses the panel, what is shown ("Species for Cell …", "Species for 2 places"), the column glossary and the CSV download. In the Species lens the Table lists the species' **model inputs** instead (with its own CSV download). In the Scores lens it opens three underline tabs: a sortable **species table** (Category, Taxon, Scientific name, Common
name, **ER code**, ER score, Model, MMPA, MBTA, Area (km²), Avg. suitability, % of category — ESA
and IUCN status are folded into ER code), a **zones table** (every Program Area ranked by the
**current layer**, with "report on selected" once some are ticked), and a **composition** treemap
(one box per species category, sized by suitability × extinction risk × area). Only the **species**
table has the phone's compact default columns and a **Columns** control; both tables get sticky
headers/first column and horizontal scrolling that never spills the panel. Only the species
table's **Download CSV** exports it; the zones table and the composition treemap have no export
yet. A drawn place's Components and Species tables in the Places results panel each have their own
working **Export CSV**.

![The Table tool's species tab. Captured on an earlier build (0.10.44); the current Table fills the whole stage beside the rail, with a single header row (← Map, the subject, Species · Zones · Composition tabs, glossary and CSV download).](/images/atlas/desktop-table.png){#fig-atlas-table fig-alt="A narrow dark panel titled Table headed Species for Cell ID 3372565 with an info and a download button, a Species, Zones and Composition switch, and a table whose Category, Taxon, Scientific name and Common name columns list birds such as Black Noddy and Sanderling, each column with a filter box."}

## Report

The **Open report** button reports **every place currently in the link** (`#pl=`); with no places,
it reports the single selected Program Area; with neither, it is disabled and the footer says "Add
a place to open a report." A row's own **Open in report** reports just that row's place. The report
opens in a new tab and renders progressively as its data arrives:

- a **header band** — mark, release chip, generation time, permalink and QR code (a restricted
  release also gets a PREVIEW banner and print watermark);
- an **introduction**;
- a collapsible **Parameters** section (kind, keys or vertices, area, cell count, study-area
  share, token);
- a **map** — interactive on screen; a static snapshot only in print and the HTML export;
- one **flower plot** per place, under "Plot of Scores";
- a **Table of Scores** — component and overall scores, with a footnote when a component covers
  under 99% of the area, or is missing entirely because the release's own 5% coverage floor
  dropped it;
- a **Summary of Species** per place (a category × count cross-tab, plus the top 20 by score);
- **Sources and Method**, with the release's own citations — each query behind these numbers is a
  parity-tested twin (`npm run parity`, max|Δ| < 1e-9) of an `msens` R function; *"Reproduce in
  R"* prints the exact calls to `msens::place_decode()`, `cells_in_polygon_grid()` and
  `scores_for_cells()` that reproduce it, needing `msens` ≥ 0.44.0 and a local copy of the
  release's `sdm.duckdb`;
- a **Provenance** section (release, status/access, app build SHA, DuckDB-WASM version, tables
  read, SQL run).

![The report document's header band and introduction: the MMA seal, a permalink and QR code, Parameters, and the start of the interactive map. Captured on an earlier build (0.10.44) and not recaptured since.](/images/atlas/desktop-report.png){#fig-atlas-report fig-alt="The report document: the Marine Minerals Administration seal and lockup, title, release chip, generation time, a real permalink and QR code, an introduction, a Parameters disclosure, and the start of the interactive map."}

![The report's Table of Scores and the start of the Summary of Species, for the same Program Area. Captured on an earlier build (0.10.44) and not recaptured since.](/images/atlas/desktop-report-scores.png){#fig-atlas-report-scores fig-alt="A flower plot legend, the Table of Scores with one row of component and overall scores, and the beginning of the Summary of Species section."}

Four exports, all built client-side: **Print** (the browser's dialog; roughly five Letter pages);
**Download HTML** (one self-contained file — the flowers stay inline SVG, only the map is an
embedded PNG); a **data package (ZIP)** — `README.md`, `CITATION.md`, `provenance.json`,
`places.geojson` (drawn/uploaded places only, not zone places), a `scores_*.csv`/`species_*.csv`
pair per place, and `query/*.sql`; and a **Word document (.docx)** — the same tables as coded Word
styles, plus the map and a rasterized flower per place.

## Accessibility and performance notes

The Atlas ships a written [WCAG 2.1 conformance note](https://github.com/MarineSensitivity/atlas/blob/main/docs/accessibility.md)
and a [performance budget report](https://github.com/MarineSensitivity/atlas/blob/main/docs/performance.md)
in its own repository. As of the note's own 0.10.24 (2026-09-23) evaluation the claim is
**"partially supports,"** not full support, and it states plainly that **no screen reader was
actually driven** in producing it — automated and manual keyboard testing stand in for that. Two
skip links sit at the very top of the page: "Skip to the tools" and "Skip to the details panel."
The critical-path JavaScript was measured (0.10.20, 2026-09-23) at **~417 KB gzip** against a
**450 KB** budget (it has been 460 KB since 0.10.89), plus **~140 KB** for the MapLibre worker
against **150 KB**; a separate gate
asserted the species lens paints its first data pixel within 2.5 s on a laptop and 4 s on CI. The
measured numbers may have moved since; see the linked reports for current ones.

## When a service is down

Since 0.10.58, the Atlas checks two external services it does not control: **titiler-v8** (every
score and species map tile) and the **S3 data origin** each release's own files are fetched from.
Both are checked at boot and on a manual **Retry**; a map tile that actually fails to load for a
real reason — a 5xx, a network error, or a timeout, never a normal "this release has no data here"
403/404 — re-checks only the tile server. It never polls in the background while everything is
fine.

When either is down, a dismissible banner — since 0.10.62 it sits in the map stage, below the top bar, so it never covers
the top bar's controls — names the failing host, the reason (timeout or HTTP
status), and what still works — places, tables and reports already built from data already loaded,
just no new tiles or new fetches from the down host; when it is specifically the **tile server**
that is down, the legend also switches to a compact **"tiles unavailable"** state instead of a bare
colour ramp. Built after titiler-v8 and the API were unreachable for an hour and the
live app kept rendering a perfectly normal-looking map with no raster and no word to anyone.

**What it cannot detect:** a partial outage (some tiles or objects failing, others not — only a
further real request surfaces it), a degraded-but-200 response (a tile that loads but paints wrong
data), or a preview session's own restricted data prefix (the probe always checks the public bucket
origin, not a signed-in override). No release the Atlas reads from calls a separate API today, so
there is nothing of that kind to probe; DuckDB-WASM's own Parquet fetches, PMTiles zone archives and
the basemap are likewise outside this check's scope — a partial CDN problem affecting only one of
those would not trip the banner.

## Feedback and versions

**Feedback** opens a dialog: a kind (bug / idea / question / data), a title, a description, an
optional email, an annotatable screenshot, and a privacy checkbox (off by default) for including
the current view's link. **Send** is live: it posts to a Google Apps Script endpoint that writes a
Sheet row, mails the team, and — for a **public** release — also files a public GitHub issue in
`MarineSensitivity/atlas` with the screenshot attached (your email, if given, is never included in
it); a **restricted** release never gets a public issue either way. An email, if given, is kept
only in the team's Sheet row and mail (plus a copy to you), never in the issue (see
`docs/feedback.md` in the atlas repo for the dialog's exact privacy wording). The original
zero-backend fallback stays alongside Send, not replaced by it: **"Open as GitHub issue"** opens
its own prefilled public issue, labelled by kind, with the screenshot copied to your clipboard to
paste in — offered on every public release whether or not Send is configured, and the only option
on a build with no endpoint set. Tell an analyst plainly: on a public release, both routes end in a
public GitHub issue. A restricted release never offers the GitHub route; on a build with no
endpoint configured it says plainly that "feedback cannot be sent from here right now."

GA4 receives interaction events as well as page views, and the app also logs those same events to
the batched usage-log Sheet the retired Shiny `scores`/`species` apps also wrote (`app = "atlas"`
distinguishes its rows) — never the URL fragment, which the app's own analytics code is
source-scanned to never read.

**Versions** follow the same public/restricted split as the rest of the MST (see @sec-releases): a
public release opens directly on the public host; a restricted pre-release's Atlas is reached only
through the signed-in preview host, at its own `/{ver}/atlas/` path. Requesting a release the
current host cannot show opens the version picker automatically: a restricted one reads, for example, "v9 is a pre-release under review and is not shown on this
host" and offers "Continue on the preview host" (a link straight to that release's Atlas there, at
`https://preview.marinesensitivity.org/v9/atlas/?ver=v9`), an unrecognized one reads "is not a version this host recognizes," and either way the promoted release loads
underneath while the picker explains why. In the picker, every public release other than the
current one offers **Switch**.

![The release picker. Captured on an earlier build (0.10.44), before v7c was published, so v7c is missing from the list.](/images/atlas/desktop-version-picker.png){#fig-atlas-versions fig-alt="A dialog titled Data release listing v7b, v9 and v8 as restricted pre-releases each with a Continue on the preview host link, v7 marked current, and v6 down to v1 marked retired, each with a Switch link and a date."}

## Known limitations (as of 0.10.91)

- In v7, 1,873 of the 2,619 `rng_iucn` range inputs have no model-asset registry row, so their pills
  in the Species lens show struck through (as they did in the retired Species Shiny app); every other
  input of v3, v6 and v7 resolves. The other pre-v8 releases (v1, v2, v4, v4b, v5, v7b, v7c) were
  not checked for this chapter.
- **GeoPackage** is refused (see the Places section above) whenever `ST_Read` fails to parse it,
  including a file with no vector layer — its declared-CRS and no-feature-table checks cannot
  actually run against an uploaded file, because DuckDB-WASM's `sqlite_scan()` cannot open a file
  registered only through `registerFileBuffer`, the way an uploaded GeoPackage is, so both checks
  silently fall through and `ST_Read`, or the normal out-of-range magnitude check, is left to catch
  a projected or empty file instead (still refused, just by a different, honest rule).
- A multi-Program-Area selection (several picks added as one place) sums area and means the
  composite for its list row, but its flower, component table and species table are not aggregated
  — the results panel asks you to select a single Program Area for those.
- **Show analysis cells** is not available for a Program Area place: the app bundle the Atlas reads
  carries each zone's count, area and scores but not its cells.
- The Atlas's report is a print-first document built and exported entirely client-side
  (HTML/ZIP/DOCX from the same source), not the retired Shiny apps' report.

## Generating Screenshots

The atlas repository's own `scripts/eyes-shots.mjs` captures the standard states most of this
chapter's figures come from (about 20 numbered shots per viewport, phone 390×844 at 2x pixel density
and desktop 1280×800, dark theme), run against a live or locally built app:

```sh
ATLAS_URL=https://marinesensitivity.org/atlas OUT=.tmp/eyes node scripts/eyes-shots.mjs
```

A few figures here (the Share dialog and its simplification ladder, the Coordinate dialog's
refusal state, the version picker, and one Report scroll position) are not among that script's own
states; they were captured by hand from the same live build, driving the app to the specific state
each caption describes. The guided-tour images of the [Atlas user guide](../apps-guide.qmd) come from
a different script, `npm run tour:guide` (`scripts/tour-guide.mjs`, from atlas 0.10.90).

## Source Code

[`atlas`](https://github.com/MarineSensitivity/atlas) on its own `main` branch — one static build
for every release, the same "one checkout, not one per version" convention the retired
[Scores](scores.qmd) and [Species](species.qmd) apps followed.
